title: st.fragment breaks sticky positioning of chat input field
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

I've run into an issue when trying to use st.fragment in combination with st.chat_input. It seems that when wrapping my simple chat logic inside a [USER].fragment, the chat input no longer sticks to the bottom of the page as expected. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# using fragment breaks sticky positioning of the chat input field

[USER].fragment
def simple_chat_test():
    st.title("Simple Chat Test")

    if "test_messages" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.test_messages = []
        st.session_state.test_messages.append({
            "role": "assistant", 
            "content": "Hi! I'm a simple test bot. I'll respond 'Got it' to everything you say. Try typing something!"
        })

    for message in st.session_state.test_messages:
        with st.chat_message(message["role"]):
            st.markdown(message["content"])

    with st.expander("Test Content (to make page longer)", expanded=False):
        for i in range(20):
            st.write(f"This is test line {i+1}")

    if prompt := st.chat_input("Type anything here..."):
        st.session_state.test_messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})
        with st.chat_message("user"):
            st.markdown(prompt)

        response = "Got it"
        st.session_state.test_messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response})
        with st.chat_message("assistant"):
            st.markdown(response)

        st.rerun()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    simple_chat_test()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Use st.fragment

### Expected Behavior

st.chat_input stays fixed to the bottom of the page (sticky), as it does when running outside of a fragment.

### Current Behavior

 The chat input is no longer sticky

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.45.0
- Python version: 3.12.1
- Operating System: Win 11
- Browser:  Chrome 137.0.7151.55


### Additional Information

_No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-11502)

Hello [USER] , thank you for filing this issue!

I can confirm that I am seeing the same behavior as you with the provided code. Thank you for providing such a great reproducible example!

As a workaround in the meantime, not using a fragment will render the chat layout as expected.

Another workaround would be to use `st._bottom.chat_input()` to enforce the chat input to be placed into the bottom container. chat input is only placed in the bottom if its used in the main page container. A fragment uses a dedicated container for its elements -> this is causing the chat input to be placed in-line. 

Related feature request to expose the bottom container as an official part of the API:  https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10722

Changing this to `enhancement` since the current behaviour is expected and unlikely to be changed. We are planning to either add an explicit `position` parameter to chat input or to expose `st.bottom` (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10722) in our public API to allow users to explicitly put a chat input to the bottom of an app. Another related issue: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8564
Closing this since the solution is to explicitly but this into the bottom container via `st.bottom.chat_input(...)` when used inside a fragment.
